{{short description|Memoryless continuous-time stochastic process that shows two distinct values}}
{{about|the probabilistic model|the electrical transmission line|Telegrapher's equations}}
In [[probability theory]], the '''telegraph process''' is a [[Memorylessness|memoryless]] continuous-time [[stochastic process]] that shows two distinct values. It models [[burst noise]] (also called popcorn noise or random telegraph signal). If the two possible values that a [[random variable]] can take are ''<math>c_1</math>'' and ''<math>c_2</math>'', then the process can be described by the following [[master equation]]s:

:<math>\partial_t P(c_1, t|x, t_0)=-\lambda_1 P(c_1, t|x, t_0)+\lambda_2 P(c_2, t|x, t_0)</math>

and

:<math>\partial_t P(c_2, t|x, t_0)=\lambda_1 P(c_1, t|x, t_0)-\lambda_2 P(c_2, t|x, t_0).</math>

where <math>\lambda_1</math> is the transition rate for going from state <math>c_1</math> to state <math>c_2</math> and <math>\lambda_2</math> is the transition rate for going from going from state <math>c_2</math> to state <math>c_1</math>. The process is also known under the names '''Kac process''' (after mathematician [[Mark Kac]]),<ref name="Kac">{{cite journal | doi = 10.1023/A:1009437108439 | last1 = Bondarenko | first1 = YV | year = 2000 | title = Probabilistic Model for Description of Evolution of Financial Indices | journal = Cybernetics and Systems Analysis | volume = 36 | issue = 5| pages = 738–742 | s2cid = 115293176 }}</ref> and '''dichotomous random process'''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Margolin | first1 = G | last2 = Barkai | first2 = E | year = 2006 | title = Nonergodicity of a Time Series Obeying Lévy Statistics | journal = Journal of Statistical Physics | volume = 122 | issue = 1| pages = 137–167 | doi =10.1007/s10955-005-8076-9 |bibcode=2006JSP...122..137M|arxiv = cond-mat/0504454 | s2cid = 53625405 }}</ref>

==Solution==
The master equation is compactly written in a matrix form by introducing a vector <math>\mathbf{P}=[P(c_1, t|x, t_0),P(c_2, t|x, t_0)]</math>,

:<math>\frac{d\mathbf P}{dt}=W\mathbf P</math>

where

:<math>W=\begin{pmatrix}
-\lambda_1 & \lambda_2 \\
\lambda_1 & -\lambda_2
\end{pmatrix}</math>

is the [[transition rate matrix]]. The formal solution is constructed from the initial condition <math>\mathbf{P}(0)</math> (that defines that at <math>t=t_0</math>, the state is <math>x</math>) by

:<math>\mathbf{P}(t) = e^{Wt}\mathbf{P}(0)</math>.

It can be shown that<ref>[[V. Balakrishnan (physicist)|Balakrishnan, V.]] (2020). Mathematical Physics: Applications and Problems. Springer International Publishing. pp. 474</ref>
:<math>e^{Wt}= I+ W\frac{(1-e^{-2\lambda t})}{2\lambda}</math>

where <math>I</math> is the identity matrix and <math>\lambda=(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)/2</math> is the average transition rate. As <math>t\rightarrow \infty</math>, the solution approaches a stationary distribution <math>\mathbf{P}(t\rightarrow \infty)=\mathbf{P}_s</math> given by

:<math>\mathbf{P}_s= \frac{1}{2\lambda}\begin{pmatrix}
\lambda_2 \\
\lambda_1
\end{pmatrix}</math>

==Properties==
Knowledge of an initial state [[exponential decay|decays exponentially]]. Therefore, for a time <math>t\gg (2\lambda)^{-1}</math>, the process will reach the following stationary values, denoted by subscript ''s'':

Mean:

: <math>\langle X \rangle_s = \frac {c_1\lambda_2+c_2\lambda_1}{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}.</math>

Variance:

: <math> \operatorname{var} \{ X \}_s = \frac {(c_1-c_2)^2\lambda_1\lambda_2}{(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)^2}.</math>

One can also calculate a [[correlation function]]:

: <math>\langle X(t),X(u)\rangle_s = e^{-2\lambda |t-u|}\operatorname{var} \{ X \}_s.</math>

==Application==

This random process finds wide application in model building:
* In [[physics]], [[Spin (physics)|spin systems]] and [[fluorescence]] [[fluorescence intermittency|intermittency]] show dichotomous properties. But especially in [[single molecule experiment]]s [[probability distribution]]s featuring [[algebraic tail]]s are used instead of the [[exponential distribution]] implied in all formulas above.
* In [[finance]] for describing [[Share capital|share]] prices<ref name="Kac" />
* In [[biology]] for describing [[transcription factor]] binding and unbinding.
